annotation_cost.rationale: Separating Recall@10 0.9 from 0.85 at 95% confidence needs 139 labeled queries. Fewer cannot evidence the SPEC threshold, the same sample-resolution rule the grounding lane applies.

reasons: Decisive tokens appear in the query for only 0.0871 of questions -- indistinguishable from the 0.087 that made PersonaMem unusable as a gate (Charter §0). Charter §3.3 says to stop here: this is the same corpus, so a curated set over it inherits the same ceiling no matter how the labels are produced.

Reference metadata localizes evidence better than random (0.4859 vs 0.0742) but below the 0.6 needed to stand in for a label, and only at a 9-message window -- that labels a region, not a claim. Recall@10 built on it would track label noise more than retrieval quality.
verdict.next_step: Source a corpus whose questions name what they ask about, then re-run this probe before annotating. Spending the annotation budget on this corpus would repeat the four interventions in Charter §0, which each improved their mechanism while the score stayed flat.
verdict.decision_is_not_engineering: Whether to spend 139 manual annotations is a cost decision, not an engineering one. This probe supplies the inputs; it deliberately does not build a set or emit labels.

scope: A pre-check, not a gate. It emits no relevance labels and computes no Recall@10 or nDCG@10; #13 and #14 stay BUILD until a curated set with admissible labels exists.
